question: In 2020, the European Union recognised ASEAN as a strategic partner and a key focal point for its broader Indo-Pacific strategy. The 2022 Strategic Compass was consistent with this by proposing a move towards closer cooperation with ASEAN in the field of conflict prevention, among others. Despite these steps, the relationship between the EU and ASEAN has not advanced further. With this in mind, 1.
What specific initiatives does the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy intend to take to deepen the relationship with ASEAN?

Why has no new plan been drawn up as a successor to the previous one after the expiry of the ASEAN and EU Action Plan for the period 2018-2022? Have there been any discussions with ASEAN on this matter or any still ongoing?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.3.2024) The Commission is continuing to strengthen the Strategic Partnership with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). The EU-ASEAN relationship has enjoyed strong political momentum over the past few years, with the elevation to a Strategic Partnership in 2020 and the first-ever summit for EU and ASEAN leaders in 2022.
Economically, the EU remains the third largest investor and the third largest trade partner for ASEAN, and a highly significant development partner.

The Commission is committed to implementing the decisions adopted by EU and ASEAN leaders at the 2022 summit, including leveraging up to EUR 10 billion in investments by Team Europe actors for Southeast Asia under the Global Gateway initiative1 and the convening of the first-ever EU-ASEAN environment ministers meeting. More recently, the EU hosted the 24th EU-ASEAN ministerial meeting on 2 February 2024 in Brussels.

The ministerial meeting provided political impetus for current work towards traderelated deliverables on green technologies and services, digital and supply chains resilience, provided an update on planning for the Global Gateway projects and funding directed to ASEAN, and exchanged views on the regional and global security situation.

The ministerial meeting also adopted a Joint Statement2, in which both sides recognised the strategic interest of holding regular leaders’ level engagement in the future. Following the expiry of the EU-ASEAN plan of action 2018-2022, a follow-up plan of action 2023-20273 to implement the Strategic Partnership was formally adopted in August 2022.
The current plan further deepens cooperation, with new work on trade, rules-based and sustainable connectivity, climate change and enhanced EU-ASEAN security cooperation.
